name: Admission to Citizenship -- Spouse of a Serbian Citizen

requirements.blocker_text: Married to a citizen of the Republic of Serbia for at least 3 years (Article 17).
requirements.fix_path: Remain married to a Serbian citizen for at least 3 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Must hold approved permanent domicile (permanent residence) in Serbia.
Written statement declaring that the applicant considers Serbia to be their own state.

evidence_required.document: Written statement recognizing Serbia as one's own state

sources.title: Paragraf.rs -- consolidated English text of the Law on Citizenship of the Republic of Serbia, Article 17: admission to citizenship for a foreigner married to a Serbian citizen for at least 3 years, holding approved permanent domicile, submitting the required statement

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Serbia). Gender-neutral on its face -- Article 17 refers to 'a foreigner married to a citizen' without specifying the sex of either spouse, unlike some other marriage-based citizenship provisions built earlier in this dataset (e.g. Morocco's Article 10). Requires holding PERMANENT residence (not merely temporary), which itself normally requires 3 years of prior temporary residence -- so, similarly to rs_naturalisation.json, the marriage route's literal 3-year marriage-duration figure can sit on top of a longer practical residence-permit timeline; not modeled as a separate hard requirement here since Article 17 itself does not state a minimum prior-residence duration, only that permanent domicile must be 'approved' at the time of application. dual_citizenship_allowed modeled null (unknown) since Article 17, unlike Article 14's naturalisation route, does not explicitly repeat the foreign-citizenship-release condition, but this was not independently confirmed either way in the source reviewed -- disclosed as a gap rather than guessed.
